newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end slightly lower, rangebound.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end slightly lower, rangebound.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended slightly lower in rangebound trade, as traders looked to next Tuesday's fourth-quarter U.S. employment cost index report.
"We are waiting until Tuesday," one bond futures trader said.
"That (the index) is maybe more important than nonfarm payrolls," another market source said.
The results of the U.S. Treasury's five-year note auction sparked some pit activity, with dealers and locals liquidating long positions.
While traders said the five-year note auction was fairly good, they said the pit was too long ahead of the auction.
"It's just a little bit of indigestion from the auction," one bond trader said about the light selloff in the pit.
Traders said a revision in the Economic Cycle Research Institute's (ECRI) U.S. inflation gauge for the week ended January 3 pushed most bonds and Eurodollars to fresh lows.
The revision lifted the January 3 index to 107.2 -- a 36-week high -- and highlighted worries about growing U.S. inflationary pressures.
March T-bonds fell to 110-20/32, with support seen at 110-11/32 and the one-week low of 110-06/32.
However, March T-bonds and June Eurodollars remain mired in 2-1/2-week trading ranges. June Eurodollars touched minor support at 94.17. Further support rests at 94.13.

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were down 06/32 at 110-27/32, 10-year notes were off 06/32 at 108-09/32, June Eurodollars were off one basis point at 94.19, September Eurodollars were off two bps at 94.01 and June T-bills were down two bps at 94.75.
